recent_posts.title: Docker Sandbox Kits: Finally, A Way to Stop Re-Doing the Same Setup
recent_posts.summary: Docker Sandbox Kits offer a reusable approach to setting up development environments, eliminating the repetitive work of configuring the same Docker-based setups from scratch each time. The concept focuses on templating or packaging common sandbox configurations so developers can quickly spin up consistent environments without redundant effort.

recent_posts.title: Why Your Platform Team Became the Bottleneck — And How to Fix It
recent_posts.summary: Platform teams built to reduce friction often become bottlenecks themselves due to DIY platform approaches that consume engineering bandwidth. The cloud-native ecosystem already has proven tools — Kubernetes, Backstage, GitOps, and observability — but organizations lose months wiring them together. The post argues that 80% of every internal developer platform is identical across organizations, making from-scratch builds wasteful. It introduces OpenChoreo, an open-source developer platform that pre-integrates these tools with sensible defaults, aiming to let platform teams skip the assembly work and focus on business-specific differentiation.

recent_posts.title: Our AWS Bill Spiked 3x Overnight — It Wasn’t Traffic, It Was One Missing Limit
recent_posts.summary: A DevOps engineer shares a postmortem of an AWS bill tripling overnight due to a runaway Auto Scaling Group. A background SQS worker with no concurrency ceiling triggered a self-amplifying feedback loop: slow jobs raised CPU, which launched more EC2 instances, which pulled more messages, which caused more retries. The fix involved setting a hard max on the ASG in Terraform, capping application-level concurrency with p-limit, adding circuit breakers for downstream failures, and setting up AWS Budget alerts and cost anomaly detection.

recent_posts.title: Taming the Infrastructure Beast: What Platform Engineering Actually Is
recent_posts.summary: Platform Engineering is the discipline of building self-service toolchains and workflows—collectively called an Internal Developer Platform (IDP)—that reduce operational toil for software developers. Unlike DevOps, which is a cultural philosophy, Platform Engineering productizes that culture by treating the IDP as an internal product with real customers (developers), measurable outcomes (deployment frequency, time to first commit), and a feedback loop. A key concept is the 'Golden Path': an opinionated, well-documented route to production that includes pre-configured CI/CD, monitoring, security guardrails, and base images. Teams can deviate from it but then own the resulting infrastructure burden themselves. The goal is to shift cognitive load away from developers so they can focus on business logic rather than infrastructure operations.

recent_posts.title: Adding Real Mobile Device Tests to Our Azure Pipeline Before Build – What I Learned
recent_posts.summary: A team integrated real mobile device testing into their Azure DevOps pipeline using BrowserStack Automate and Percy to catch UI issues before releases. The automated tests run before builds complete, reducing manual testing overhead and increasing confidence. Key challenges included slow device performance (especially iOS), difficult pipeline debugging, and intermittent failures from network or device issues. The approach complements rather than replaces manual testing.

recent_posts.title: Need for Speed: Nixopus Deploys 4 Services in just 300 Seconds.
recent_posts.summary: Nixopus is an open-source platform that simplifies self-hosting and server management through an integrated web terminal, one-click containerized deployments, and a visual file manager. The platform eliminates repetitive configuration tasks and provides a browser-based interface for server operations, replacing traditional SSH clients and command-line file transfers.

recent_posts.title: Raspberry Pi (k3s) Monitoring: Prometheus + Grafana, the Pi-friendly way
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide for setting up a complete monitoring stack on Raspberry Pi using k3s, Prometheus, and Grafana. The setup is specifically optimized for low-resource hardware, demonstrating how to deploy kube-prometheus-stack with proper resource constraints and configurations suitable for ARM-based edge devices.

recent_posts.title: Sharing a n8n flow to monitor SSL expiration and SSL validation
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive n8n workflow for automated SSL certificate monitoring that combines dual verification using both a custom SSL scanner and external API. The system performs daily checks for certificate expiration, security vulnerabilities, protocol support, and compliance standards, delivering color-coded Discord notifications with detailed health assessments and A+ to F grading.

recent_posts.title: What are your most annoying false alerts of incidents? And how to avoid it?
recent_posts.summary: A DevOps/SRE professional with 10+ years of experience shares common false alert scenarios that can lead to alert fatigue and missed real incidents. Examples include staging environment alerts at 3 AM, CPU usage alerts during scheduled backups, and third-party service maintenance notifications. The post provides practical strategies to reduce false positives: using different alert channels for different services, performing comprehensive health checks, documenting and reconfiguring problematic alerts, and monitoring third-party service status.

recent_posts.title: Why does IT incidents always happen at the worst times?
recent_posts.summary: A DevOps/SRE professional shares personal experiences of IT incidents that consistently occurred during inconvenient times over a 10-year career. The incidents include disk space issues during team retreats, database mishaps during supervisor absence, WordPress security breaches at 3 AM, and SSL certificate expiration during illness. Each incident provides practical lessons about backup procedures, security hardening, network monitoring, and proactive certificate management.
